question: What is the impact of story 015-resource-time-buffer (BufferMinutes on ResourceType + Resources lifecycle events) on the current codebase?
claim:
MODULE: Resources — touched; ResourceType entity, ResourceInstance entity, and 6 command handlers (Create/Update/Delete for both types and instances) are in scope.
MODULE: Shared.Abstractions — touched, crossed-boundary; new event contracts must be added under Events/Resources/ (constitution Art. IV), the only existing coupling mechanism between modules.
MODULE: Availability — referenced by the story's intent but does not exist in the codebase today (capability-map.json lists only ManagementGroups, Resources, Users); the consuming side of the new events has no module to land in yet. Story explicitly puts Availability's own handling out of scope.
ENTITY: ResourceType (Resources.Core.Domain.ResourceType) — has no BufferMinutes property today; would need a new field plus Create/Update signature changes.
ENTITY: ResourceInstance (Resources.Core.Domain.ResourceInstance) — structurally unaffected; its Create/Delete command handlers must gain event publication.
ENDPOINT: POST /resources/types (Create resource type) — request/command must carry BufferMinutes (AC-1) and handler must publish ResourceSchemaCreatedEvent after SaveChangesAsync (AC-3); today it has neither.
ENDPOINT: PUT /resources/types/{id} (Update resource type) — request/command must carry BufferMinutes (AC-1); no publish requirement in AC.
ENDPOINT: GET /resources/types and GET /resources/types/{id} — response DTOs must include BufferMinutes (AC-2); today they do not.
ENDPOINT: DELETE /resources/types/{id} (Delete resource type) — handler must publish ResourceSchemaDeletedEvent (AC-5); today it publishes nothing.
ENDPOINT: POST /resources/instances (Create resource instance) — handler must publish ResourceInstanceCreatedEvent (AC-4); today it publishes nothing.
ENDPOINT: DELETE /resources/instances/{id} (Delete resource instance) — handler must publish ResourceInstanceDeletedEvent (AC-6); today it publishes nothing.
SCREEN: frontend/src/app/features/schemas/schemas.routes.ts (routes "new", ":schemaId") — existing screens consume resource-schema data, but the story explicitly marks frontend changes out of scope, so no screen change is required by this story.
EVENT: none exist yet — Shared.Abstractions/Events/ only has ManagementGroups/ and Users/ subfolders, no Resources/ subfolder; new contracts needed: ResourceSchemaCreatedEvent, ResourceInstanceCreatedEvent, ResourceSchemaDeletedEvent, ResourceInstanceDeletedEvent.
SCHEMA: likely change — ResourceType has no BufferMinutes column in its current EF configuration/entity; a new EF migration in Resources.Migrations is required per constitution Art. VI.
BLOCKED_BY: Availability module does not exist in the codebase (capability-map.json modules = ManagementGroups, Resources, Users only) — acceptable per the story's own out-of-scope note (consumer side is a separate story), but flagged as a fact since the new events will have zero subscribers until Availability is built.
BLOCKED_BY: the BufferMinutes upper validation limit is not defined anywhere in the codebase or the story text (AC-1 only says "reasonable upper limit"); epic open decision no. 3 (source of truth for the buffer: Resources vs Availability) is explicitly still open per the story frontmatter.
RISK: DeleteResourceTypeCommandHandler soft-deletes a schema's instances via a bulk ExecuteUpdateAsync (SoftDeleteInstancesAsync), not through ResourceInstance.Delete() — so instances belonging to a deleted schema will not individually raise ResourceInstanceDeletedEvent; only ResourceSchemaDeletedEvent fires for the schema itself.
RISK: GroupDeletedHandler hard-deletes all ResourceTypes for a group via a bulk ExecuteDeleteAsync — confirmed no per-schema ResourceSchemaDeletedEvent will be published on group deletion; this matches the story's stated out-of-scope design (Availability must react to GroupDeleted separately) but is a real behavioural gap if not handled.
RISK: no new authorization gap identified — CreateResourceTypeCommandHandler already enforces group.OwnerId == command.CallerId for schema creation; adding BufferMinutes to existing create/update paths does not introduce a new authz surface (consistent with story's touches_authz: false).

question: Describe exactly what the following Resources handlers do, with file:line excerpts: DeleteResourceTypeCommandHandler (does it soft-delete instances, hard-delete the type, in what order, and is there a single SaveChangesAsync or several), DeleteResourceInstanceCommandHandler or equivalent (soft or hard delete), and GroupDeletedHandler (how it deletes types/instances, whether via ExecuteDeleteAsync, and whether SaveChangesAsync is called). claim:
DeleteResourceTypeCommandHandler (backend/src/Modules/Resources/ThingsBooksy.Modules.Resources.Core/Features/DeleteResourceType/DeleteResourceTypeCommandHandler.cs) first soft-deletes all resource instances of the type via a bulk ExecuteUpdateAsync (IDeleteResourceTypeCommandDataProvider.SoftDeleteInstancesAsync, which sets DeletedAt/UpdatedAt and bypasses the query filter with IgnoreQueryFilters), then removes the ResourceType entity from the DbSet (RemoveResourceType, EF-tracked hard delete, relying on DB cascade for ResourcePropertyDefinitions), and finally calls SaveChangesAsync exactly once. The bulk ExecuteUpdateAsync executes immediately/independently of SaveChangesAsync (it is its own SQL statement), so there is one explicit SaveChangesAsync call in the handler (for the RemoveResourceType tracked-entity delete), after the instances have already been soft-deleted by the bulk update. Order: (1) soft-delete instances via ExecuteUpdateAsync, (2) hard-delete the type via tracked Remove + single SaveChangesAsync.

DeleteResourceInstanceCommandHandler (backend/src/Modules/Resources/ThingsBooksy.Modules.Resources.Core/Features/DeleteResourceInstance/DeleteResourceInstanceCommandHandler.cs) performs a SOFT delete: it loads the tracked ResourceInstance entity, calls the domain method instance.Delete(_clock.CurrentDate()) (which sets DeletedAt, per ResourceInstance.cs:46), then calls _dataProvider.SaveChangesAsync once. No hard delete/ExecuteDeleteAsync is used.

GroupDeletedHandler (backend/src/Modules/Resources/ThingsBooksy.Modules.Resources.Core/Events/Handlers/GroupDeletedHandler.cs) is an IEventHandler<GroupDeleted> reacting to a group-deleted domain event from ManagementGroups. It: (1) soft-deletes all ResourceInstances for the group via a bulk ExecuteUpdateAsync (IgnoreQueryFilters + Where DeletedAt==null, SetProperty DeletedAt/UpdatedAt to now) — this is a direct SQL bulk statement, not a SaveChangesAsync-tracked save; (2) hard-deletes all ResourceTypes for the group via ExecuteDeleteAsync (also IgnoreQueryFilters, no Where on DeletedAt, comment states DB cascade removes ResourcePropertyDefinitions) — also a direct bulk SQL statement; (3) then looks up the GroupReadModel by Id, and only if found, removes it from the tracked DbSet and calls _dbContext.SaveChangesAsync(cancellationToken) once (line 46) — this is the only explicit SaveChangesAsync call in this handler, and it only fires conditionally when a GroupReadModel row exists (idempotent null guard).

Report: whether FluentValidation or another validator library is used (csproj reference file:line), where validators live (file paths), one example validator with an integer range rule if any exists (file:line excerpt), how a validation failure is turned into an HTTP response (status code, body shape - file:line), and the domain exception types available in Resources (file names). claim: No validator library (FluentValidation or otherwise) is referenced anywhere in the backend csproj files searched (Resources.Api, Resources.Core, Shared.Infrastructure, Shared.Abstractions all lack such a reference; a repo-wide search for 'FluentValidation' under backend/ returned no matches). Instead, both the Resources and ManagementGroups modules validate inline inside their MediatR-style command/query handlers (e.g. CreateResourceInstanceCommandHandler.cs, CreateResourceTypeCommandHandler.cs, UpdateManagementGroupCommandHandler.cs) using manual `if`/guard checks that throw module-specific CustomException subtypes (ResourcesDomainException / ManagementGroupsDomainException) — there is no separate 'Validator' class or folder in either module. The single exception is one DataAnnotations use: AddGroupMemberCommandHandler.cs uses `EmailAddressAttribute` (System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations) to check email format. An integer range rule exists as a `Math.Clamp` (not a rejecting validator) on the pagination 'take' parameter in GetResourceInstancesQueryHandler.cs — MinTake=1, MaxTake=50, DefaultTake=20, clamped rather than throwing on out-of-range input. A validation/domain failure becomes an HTTP response via ErrorHandlerMiddleware.cs, which catches all exceptions, resolves them through IExceptionCompositionRoot -> IExceptionToResponseMapper (module-specific mapper first, falling back to the shared default ExceptionToResponseMapper.cs), and writes `context.Response.StatusCode` + `WriteAsJsonAsync(response)`. The shared default mapper maps: NotFoundException -> 404, ForbiddenException -> 403, any other CustomException (including ResourcesDomainException/ManagementGroupsDomainException) -> 400 BadRequest, with body shape `{ Errors: [ { Code, Message } ] }` (record ErrorsResponse(params Error[] Errors), Error(Code, Message)). Resources also has a module-specific mapper (ResourcesExceptionToResponseMapper.cs) that maps ResourceTypeNameAlreadyExistsException to 409 Conflict with body `{ code = "RESOURCE_TYPE_NAME_TAKEN", message }`. Domain exception types present in Resources (by file name, folder backend/src/Modules/Resources/ThingsBooksy.Modules.Resources.Core/Exceptions/): ResourcesDomainException.cs, ResourcesForbiddenException.cs, ResourcesExceptionToResponseMapper.cs, ResourceTypeNameAlreadyExistsException.cs (no NotFoundException-derived type exists for Resources per core-surface.json and per file listing). Regarding the Create factory: the Create factories themselves (e.g. ResourceType.Create, ResourcePropertyDefinition.Create, ResourceInstance.Create) contain NO validation/guard logic — they are simple object initializers with no throw statements. Rejection of invalid input happens earlier, in the calling command handler, before Create is invoked, via `throw new ResourcesDomainException(...)` (e.g. CreateResourceInstanceCommandHandler.cs:38 'Instance name cannot be empty.' before ResourceInstance.Create is called at line 68; CreateResourceTypeCommandHandler.cs:30 similar for resource type name).

question: How integration tests can observe a published event, and how the broker is configured under test
claim: ThingsBooksyWebAppFactory does not register any test-specific IMessageBroker/IOutboxBroker/IAsyncMessageDispatcher override; it only overrides postgres connection string, logger console/file flags, and management-groups/resources module-enabled flags via an in-memory config source, so the production DI registrations from AddMessaging/AddOutbox apply unchanged in tests. Messaging config comes from appsettings.json keys 'messaging:useAsyncDispatcher' (true) and 'outbox:enabled' (false, plus 'outbox:interval'), bound to MessagingOptions/OutboxOptions; appsettings.Development.json and appsettings.Docker.json only override postgres/logger keys, not messaging/outbox, and ThingsBooksyWebAppFactory's in-memory overrides also do not touch them — so tests run with outbox disabled and the async in-process dispatcher enabled. Because outbox is disabled, InMemoryMessageBroker.PublishAsync skips IOutboxBroker.SendAsync (outboxBroker.Enabled is false) and instead calls IAsyncMessageDispatcher.PublishAsync, which writes to an in-process Channel consumed by a hosted AsyncDispatcherJob; EfOutbox.SaveAsync (which would populate the Outbox DbSet) early-returns with a warning when Enabled is false, so Outbox/Inbox DbSets are not populated in the current test flow — no code path writes an OutboxMessage row while outbox:enabled=false. No test project registers a test-only IEventHandler<T>, message sink, or collector to capture published events; grepping for IEventHandler< and IMessageBroker in *IntegrationTests*/*Tests* projects only turns up production event handlers (GroupCreatedHandler, GroupDeletedHandler, GroupMemberAddedHandler, GroupMemberRemovedHandler, UserSignedUpHandler) and decorators, plus test code that (a) resolves the real IEventHandler<GroupDeleted> from DI and invokes it directly (GroupDeletedHandlerTests.InvokeHandlerAsync), or (b) polls read-model DB tables populated by the real async-dispatched handlers (GroupReadModelEventHandlerTests, EventPublishingTests use a WaitUntilAsync poll loop of up to 3-6 seconds against ResourcesDbContext read models) as the observable proof that an event was published/handled — there is no dedicated event-capturing sink. The Resources IntegrationTests are structured as: TestClient class ResourcesTestClient (wraps ManagementGroups HTTP calls plus ResourcesDbContext query helpers), a user factory ResourcesUserFactory (inserts a management_groups.user_read_models row via raw SQL and mints a JWT, no cross-module type import) and a data-seeding factory ResourcesGroupReadModelFactory (writes GroupReadModel/GroupMemberReadModel rows directly via ResourcesDbContext, bypassing the event pipeline), and an IntegrationTestCollection collection-fixture definition binding ThingsBooksyWebAppFactory via ICollectionFixture.

question: Uniqueness check and soft-delete interactions for ResourceType
claim: 1) ExistsByGroupAndNameAsync in both CreateResourceType and UpdateResourceType data providers calls `.IgnoreQueryFilters()` (bypassing the global DeletedAt==null query filter) but re-applies an explicit `t.DeletedAt == null` predicate in the same LINQ expression, so the net effect is that soft-deleted rows are excluded from the uniqueness check just as the global filter would exclude them — but the check itself never sees deleted-row data implicitly, it's explicit. 2) The unique index on resource_types(GroupId, Name), defined both in ResourceTypeConfiguration.cs and in migration 20260514155140_AddResourceTypeUniqueAndCursorIndexes.cs and reflected in the model snapshot, is NOT filtered (no HasFilter/filter argument) — it is a plain `.IsUnique()` index covering all rows regardless of DeletedAt. This differs from resource_instances(GroupId, Id) and management_groups(OwnerId, Name), which both use `HasFilter("\"DeletedAt\" IS NULL")` partial unique/lookup indexes. 3) IgnoreQueryFilters() call sites on ResourceTypes in Resources.Core (non-test) code: CreateResourceTypeCommandDataProvider.ExistsByGroupAndNameAsync (duplicate-name check, explicitly re-filters DeletedAt==null), UpdateResourceTypeCommandDataProvider.ExistsByGroupAndNameAsync (same pattern), and DeleteResourceTypeCommandDataProvider.SoftDeleteInstancesAsync which calls IgnoreQueryFilters on ResourceInstances (not ResourceTypes) to reach already non-deleted instances for cascading soft-delete, filtering `DeletedAt == null` explicitly. No other ResourceTypes.IgnoreQueryFilters() call sites exist in Resources.Core; GroupDeletedHandler.cs uses IgnoreQueryFilters on GroupReadModels/GroupMemberReadModels, not ResourceTypes. GetResourceInstancesQueryDataProvider uses IgnoreQueryFilters conditionally on ResourceInstances for an includeDeleted query option, unrelated to ResourceType. 4) CreateResourceInstanceCommandHandler resolves the resource type via `_dataProvider.GetResourceTypeAsync(command.ResourceTypeId, ct)`, and CreateResourceInstanceCommandDataProvider.GetResourceTypeAsync does `_dbContext.ResourceTypes.FirstOrDefaultAsync(t => t.Id == resourceTypeId, ct)` with NO IgnoreQueryFilters — so it goes through the global HasQueryFilter(x => x.DeletedAt == null), meaning a soft-deleted ResourceType (DeletedAt set) would return null from this query and be treated as 'Resource type not found.' by the handler. 5) Critical finding contradicting a soft-delete assumption: DELETE /resources/types/{id} is actually a HARD delete of the ResourceType row — DeleteResourceTypeCommandDataProvider.RemoveResourceType calls `_dbContext.ResourceTypes.Remove(resourceType)` (EF Remove, not a DeletedAt update), while its associated ResourceInstances are soft-deleted via SoftDeleteInstancesAsync's ExecuteUpdateAsync setting DeletedAt. Integration tests UpdateDeleteResourceTypeTests.cs explicitly assert the type row is gone 'even with IgnoreQueryFilters()' after delete (lines 185, 283), confirming hard delete despite ResourceType having a DeletedAt/IsDeleted property and a HasQueryFilter configured. 6) No integration test was found in ThingsBooksy.Modules.Resources.IntegrationTests that deletes a ResourceType and then asserts about the row's continued existence (soft-delete state) or re-creates a type with the same name after deletion; the closest related tests only cover duplicate-name-in-same-group (409), same-name-in-different-group (201/Created), and same-name-as-itself-on-update (success) — none re-create after delete. 7) One filtered/partial unique index pattern (HasIndex(...).HasFilter(...)) exists in the solution within the read paths available: ManagementGroupConfiguration.cs `builder.HasIndex(g => new { g.OwnerId, g.Name }).IsUnique().HasFilter("\"DeletedAt\" IS NULL")`, and ResourceInstanceConfiguration.cs uses a non-unique filtered index `HasIndex(i => new { i.GroupId, i.Id }).HasFilter("\"DeletedAt\" IS NULL")`. The ResourceType unique index (GroupId, Name) is the one index on these two entities that is NOT filtered.

notes: Answer covers all six sub-questions in Question 7. Note the surprising finding (5): DELETE /resources/types/{id} performs a hard delete of the ResourceType row (EF Remove) even though ResourceType has DeletedAt/IsDeleted and a query filter — only ResourceInstances are soft-deleted in the cascade. This means the uniqueness-index-vs-soft-delete question is somewhat moot for ResourceType itself since deleted rows are physically removed, not left behind with DeletedAt set; the unfiltered unique index on (GroupId, Name) therefore only constrains live rows in practice today, but would block re-use of a name by a soft-deleted (not yet hard-deleted) row if ResourceType.Delete() is ever called without RemoveResourceType (no such path was found in the read code). Item 5 (test that deletes then re-creates same name) — no such test found in Resources.IntegrationTests; only duplicate-name (409), cross-group same-name, and same-name-on-self-update scenarios exist.
